turn.speech: Kleinkünstler, a Postgres role is a card holder in the house system. With login it acts like a user, without login like a group that holds permissions. Question: if a role named reader has no LOGIN but has SELECT on a table, can a client connect as reader, and is it still useful?
turn.text:
Kleinkünstler, I'm the Känguru. I live here rent-free, and I'll be teaching you to debug Supabase and PostgreSQL like a support engineer. Plan: baseline case, check your macOS prerequisites, start a disposable CLI lab, then trace one request from client to PostgREST to Postgres to GRANT to RLS to table. First, your question.

Think of the WG as a house with one key-card system. A role is a card holder on that system. The same card type can be a person (Alice, who can open the front door) or a function ("the cleaning rota", who can't open the door but whose permissions get handed to whoever joins). Where this stops being valid: real keys don't nest. Postgres roles can be members of other roles, and the member can inherit privileges.

Technically, Postgres has one concept, the role. A role with login privileges works as a "user". A role without login works as a "group" that holds permissions for several users [1]. Roles can be granted privileges like `SELECT`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE` and `DELETE` on tables, views, functions and other objects through `GRANT` [2]. Supabase's docs also say these roles mostly configure system access, while application access should go through Row Level Security [3].

Supabase uses a few roles you'll meet constantly:

| Role | What the docs say it is for |
|---|---|
| `anon` | Unauthenticated access. PostgREST uses it when the user is not signed in [4]. |
| `authenticated` | Signed-in access [5]. |
| `service_role` | Elevated access. PostgREST uses it to bypass RLS [6]. Never expose it client-side [7]. |
| `postgres` | The default admin role [8]. |

I haven't run anything yet. In the lab we'll look at `pg_roles` with real output, not my description of it.

Here is your first task. Suppose a role named `reader` is created with no `LOGIN` attribute, and it has `SELECT` on a table. Can a client connect to the database as `reader`? Could the role still be useful? Answer both, and take your time. I'll go check whether the pralinen are still there.
